analysis.title: GATX Corp. (GATX): 3Q26 EPS Beat; 2026 EPS Expected to Exceed Top-End of Prior Guide; Remain Buy-Rated
key_insights: GATX reported 3Q26 operating EPS of $2.92 versus $2.46 Visible Alpha consensus and $2.50 GSe. Revenue was $598M, 1.7% above GSe and 0.8% above consensus.
Beat drivers: gains on sale of $52M vs $50M GSe, SG&A of $65M vs $68M GSe, and North America Rail segment profit of $121M vs $100M GSe.
GATX raised 2026 guidance to EPS modestly above the high end of the prior $9.90-$10.30 range. Pre-print consensus was $10.23 and GSe was $10.30. GSe is now $10.40.
GS reiterates Buy and raises the 12-month price target to $232 from $223 against a $168.87 price (37.4% upside). EPS estimates for FY26/27/28 rise to $10.40/$11.40/$12.35 from $10.30/$11.15/$12.10.

Buy thesis: (1) strong railcar leasing fundamentals including aftermarket gains on sale, where market values exceed depreciated book values, (2) balanced to tighter railcar supply/demand over the next 12-18 months with muted new railcar deliveries in 2026, (3) synergies and EPS accretion from the closed Brookfield/Wells Fargo railcar fleet deal.

Wells Fargo deal synergies are running on pace to double the original 20-30 cent target for 2026. Management expects modest accretion in Year 1 and more significant accretion afterward. GATX holds call options to acquire the JV, so its share of the fleet can rise.

North America Rail segment margin was 27.1% vs 23.1% GSe, helped by higher revenue, lower maintenance and depreciation expense, and higher gains on sale. International Rail margin was 33.1% vs 33.7% GSe.

Engine leasing missed: core gross profit was $17M vs $20M GSe and segment profit including affiliates was $51M vs $63M GSe, mainly on lower other income. Share of affiliate earnings was $46M vs $42M GSe.

North America fleet utilization rose to 98.4% in 3Q from about 98% in 2Q and 1Q. The Lease Price Index was +12.4% vs +17% in 2Q and +22% in 1Q. Lease rates on renewals are still rising but moderating with mix and the Wells Fargo cars.
Utilization was 99.0% for GATX and 96.5% for Wells Fargo at the time of the acquisition, so the lower combined figure is consistent with management's expectations.
New railcar prices are rising on input cost inflation and section 232 tariffs on tank cars. GS says this supports values of existing fleets, favoring the largest lease fleets like GATX.
GS rates GATX Buy above the manufacturing-exposed peers TRN (Neutral) and GBX (Sell), citing near-term manufacturing headwinds outweighing solid leasing fundamentals.
Aircraft spare engine leasing, including the Rolls-Royce JV, benefits from constrained aircraft supply and an aged post-Covid fleet.
GS expects estimate revisions to skew upward. 4Q estimates were lowered slightly for the timing of gains on sale.

earnings_insights: GATX 3Q26 recurring EPS reported $2.92 vs Visible Alpha consensus est $2.46 and GSe $2.50.
3Q26 revenue reported $598M vs GSe $588M and consensus $593M.
3Q26 net gain on asset dispositions reported $52M vs GSe $50M. North America gains were $50M vs $48M GSe.
3Q26 North America Rail segment profit reported $121M vs GSe $100M. Segment margin 27.1% vs 23.1% GSe.
3Q26 engine leasing segment profit reported $51M vs GSe $63M, and core gross profit $17M vs GSe $20M.
FY26 guidance raised to EPS modestly above the prior $9.90-$10.30 range. Pre-print consensus est $10.23, GSe was $10.30 and is now $10.40.
Price target uses a 17.7x/16.2x/19.2x P/E on base/bear/bull Q5-Q8 EPS of $12.42/$9.04/$16.00, weighted 50/30/20%.

trade_ideas.description: Buy GATX with a 12-month price target of $232
trade_ideas.rationale: Railcar leasing fundamentals, elevated gains on sale and Wells Fargo fleet synergies support upward EPS revisions.
trade_ideas.risk: Lease rates, fleet growth or utilization below estimates, weaker secondary market sales, a poor Rolls-Royce JV contribution, or higher expenses.

risk_factors: Lease rates, fleet growth or utilization come in below estimates because of industry overbuilding without sustainable demand.
Slowing customer renewals or limited industrial production growth limits fleet growth and utilization.
Gains on sale of railcars and aircraft spare engines come in below estimates because of lower sale prices or fewer units sold.
The 50/50 aircraft spare engine leasing JV with Rolls-Royce contributes less to earnings than expected.
Expenses run higher than forecast, producing lower margins.
